key_insight: Patients at highest risk of having their training-set membership exposed remained largely consistent across tested medical AI configurations, enabling lightweight early screening.
clinical_relevance: Screening during data preparation could flag patient records at elevated privacy risk that cohort-average assessments may obscure.
method: Measured patient-level vulnerability to membership inference attacks across training configurations.
Tested how weight decay, architectures and initializations affected exposure risk.
Developed a screening tool using four small models before production-model training.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered 7,789 models across six clinical datasets and four modalities, including two adapted pretrained medical models; stronger weight decay reduced the exposed cohort up to threefold.
watch_item: Screening flags potential vulnerability rather than guaranteeing privacy protection; performance beyond the tested datasets and configurations remains uncertain.
paper_title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
